ports.name: i_tx_valid
ports.meaning: Transmit stream: i_tx_data holds a byte to send

ports.name: o_tx_ready
ports.meaning: Transmit stream: the transmitter can accept a byte at the next edge

ports.name: i_tx_data
ports.meaning: Transmit stream: byte to send; bit 0 is sent first

ports.name: o_rx_valid
ports.meaning: Receive stream: the holding register holds a byte

ports.name: i_rx_ready
ports.meaning: Receive stream: the consumer takes the held byte at this edge

ports.name: o_rx_data
ports.meaning: Receive stream: received byte; bit 0 was received first; qualified by o_rx_valid

ports.name: o_rx_frame_err
ports.meaning: Receive stream: 1 when the stop bit of the held byte was sampled as 0; qualified by o_rx_valid

ports.name: o_rx_overrun
ports.meaning: One-cycle pulse: a received byte was dropped because the holding register was full

ports.name: i_rxd
ports.meaning: Serial receive line, idle high, asynchronous to i_clk, synchronised inside the block

checks.title: Outputs change only at rising i_clk edges (no combinational input-to-output path)
checks.behavior: Between two consecutive rising edges of i_clk, while i_rst_n stays 1, none of o_tx_ready, o_txd, o_rx_valid, o_rx_data, o_rx_frame_err or o_rx_overrun may change value. Outputs are sampled just after each rising edge settles and again just before the next rising edge (including at the falling edge of i_clk, where tests change i_tx_valid, i_tx_data, i_rx_ready and i_rxd). Any output change outside a rising edge of i_clk or a falling edge of i_rst_n is a failure.

checks.title: Output values while reset is asserted
checks.behavior: While i_rst_n=0 the outputs must be o_txd=1, o_tx_ready=1, o_rx_valid=0, o_rx_data=8'h00, o_rx_frame_err=0, o_rx_overrun=0. This is checked at every rising edge of i_clk where i_rst_n=0. It is also checked right after each falling edge of i_rst_n (after a delta/settle, before the next rising edge of i_clk), so the outputs must take these values without waiting for an i_clk edge.

checks.title: Transmitter accepts a byte at the first edge after reset release
checks.behavior: Let R1 be the first rising edge of i_clk with i_rst_n=1 after one or more edges with i_rst_n=0. Just before R1, o_tx_ready must be 1. If i_tx_valid=1 at R1, then in the cycle after R1 o_txd=0 (start bit) and o_tx_ready=0. If i_tx_valid=0 at R1, then in the cycle after R1 o_txd=1 and o_tx_ready=1.

checks.title: o_rx_overrun is a one-cycle pulse and the held byte is kept
checks.behavior: If o_rx_overrun=1 in the cycle after rising edge E, then: (a) at E, o_rx_valid=1, i_rx_ready=0 and i_rst_n=1; (b) in the cycle after E, o_rx_valid=1 and o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err equal their values in the cycle before E (dropped byte and its frame-error flag not visible); (c) o_rx_overrun=0 in the cycle after edge E+1.

checks.title: Held byte stays stable until taken
checks.behavior: If o_rx_valid=1, i_rx_ready=0 and i_rst_n=1 at rising edge E, then in the cycle after E o_rx_valid=1, and o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err are unchanged from the cycle before E.

checks.title: Take without new load clears o_rx_valid
checks.behavior: If o_rx_valid=1, i_rx_ready=1 and i_rst_n=1 at rising edge E, then o_rx_overrun=0 in the cycle after E. If E is not a delivery edge V of the RX reference model (CHK-008), then in the cycle after E o_rx_valid=0, and o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err are unchanged. If E is a delivery edge V, then in the cycle after E o_rx_valid=1 and o_rx_data/o_rx_frame_err hold the new frame.

checks.title: o_rx_data/o_rx_frame_err change only when a byte is loaded
checks.behavior: If i_rst_n=1 at rising edge E and o_rx_data or o_rx_frame_err in the cycle after E differs from the cycle before E, then o_rx_valid=1 in the cycle after E and E is a delivery edge V where the RX model loads a byte. If o_rx_valid=0 in the cycle after E, then o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err equal their values before E. From reset release until the first load they are 8'h00 and 0.

checks.title: Cycle-accurate RX reference model scoreboard
checks.behavior: Model: s(E) = i_rxd sampled at rising edge E, with s(R1-1)=1 at the first edge R1 after reset release. Let N=PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT and H=floor(N/2). The model is either idle or receiving. When idle (and i_rst_n=1), it detects T0=E if and only if s(E-1)=1 and s(E)=0. At T0+H, if s(T0+H)=1 it returns to idle (glitch). Otherwise data bit i (i=0..7) = s(T0+H+(i+1)N), the stop sample is s(M) with M=T0+H+9N, and the model is idle again from M (so detection is possible at M+1). Other samples are ignored. At delivery edge V=M+2: if o_rx_valid=0, or o_rx_valid=1 with i_rx_ready=1, the model loads (valid=1, data=byte, ferr=NOT s(M), overrun=0). If o_rx_valid=1 with i_rx_ready=0, the model drops (state unchanged, overrun=1 for the cycle after V). At other edges: if valid=1 and i_rx_ready=1 then valid=0; overrun=0. i_rx_ready is ignored when valid=0. Asserting i_rst_n=0 clears all model state, including pending frames and deliveries. Check: in the cycle after every rising edge, o_rx_valid, o_rx_data, o_rx_frame_err and o_rx_overrun must equal the model.

checks.title: Cycle-exact transmit frame on o_txd
checks.behavior: TX model: a handshake happens at rising edge E0 when i_tx_valid=1, o_tx_ready=1 and i_rst_n=1 at E0. The model then records D = i_tx_data sampled at E0. For every k from 0 to 10N-1, where N=PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT, o_txd in the cycle after edge E0+k must equal F(floor(k/N)), with F(0)=0, F(j)=D[j-1] for j=1..8 and F(9)=1. So each frame bit lasts exactly N consecutive cycles and the start bit begins in the first cycle after E0. A new handshake at E0+10N starts its own frame from that edge, with no idle cycle in between. The check is abandoned if i_rst_n falls before the frame ends. i_tx_data at any edge other than E0 must not change the frame.

checks.title: o_tx_ready timing after a handshake
checks.behavior: After a handshake at edge E0 (as defined in CHK-009), and while i_rst_n stays 1: o_tx_ready=0 in the cycles after edges E0, E0+1, ..., E0+10N-2 (exactly 10N-1 cycles), and o_tx_ready=1 in the cycle after edge E0+10N-1. So no handshake is possible at edges E0+1 to E0+10N-1.

checks.title: Idle transmitter drives o_txd=1 and o_tx_ready=1
checks.behavior: The TX model is idle after rising edge E (with i_rst_n=1) when no handshake happened at any edge from E-10N+1 to E since the last reset release. In every cycle after such an edge E, o_txd=1 and o_tx_ready=1. This includes the period from E0+10N until the next handshake when no byte is accepted at E0+10N.

checks.title: No byte accepted without a full handshake
checks.behavior: At a rising edge E where i_tx_valid=0, or o_tx_ready=0, or i_rst_n=0, no frame starts. o_txd and o_tx_ready in the cycle after E must equal the TX model prediction from earlier handshakes only: o_txd=1 and o_tx_ready=1 if idle; otherwise the next bit of the frame already in progress. That prediction is independent of i_tx_data and i_tx_valid at E. Stimulus drives random i_tx_data every cycle and i_tx_valid=1 during busy and reset periods, so a wrong acceptance or a wrong data capture shows up as a mismatch.

checks.title: CFG-MIN regression, PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=4
checks.behavior: The design works at the smallest bit period (N=4, H=2).
checks.stimulus: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=4. Run, in one simulation: transmit patterns plus back-to-back traffic; receive patterns plus back-to-back traffic; the sampling-point test (correct value only at T0+2+4(i+1) and at M=T0+38, inverted at the neighbouring edges); glitches of 1 and 2 samples and an accepted 3-sample pulse; loopback; overrun. All assertions are enabled.
checks.expected: Each transmit frame bit lasts 4 cycles, and o_tx_ready=0 for 39 cycles after each handshake. Each receive delivery is at T0+2+36+2=T0+40. Glitches of 1 and 2 samples are rejected, and a 3-sample pulse gives 8'hFF. Loopback latency is E0+41. Overrun behaves as in CHK-028. CHK-001..CHK-012 pass in every cycle.

checks.title: CFG-WIDE regression, PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=1024
checks.behavior: The design works with a wide bit counter (N=1024, H=512).
checks.stimulus: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=1024. 6 transmit frames (2 back to back), 6 receive frames (2 back to back), the sampling-point test for 2 bytes, glitches of 512 samples (rejected) and 513 samples (accepted), and 1 loopback byte.
checks.expected: Each transmit bit lasts 1024 cycles and o_tx_ready=0 for 10239 cycles. Receive delivery is at T0+512+9216+2. The 512-sample glitch is rejected and the 513-sample pulse gives 8'hFF with o_rx_frame_err=0. Loopback delivery is at E0+9731. All assertions pass.

checks.title: Maximum bit period, PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=65535
checks.behavior: Bit-period and sample-offset counting do not overflow or wrap early at N=65535 (H=32767).
checks.stimulus: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=65535. Send transmit byte 8'hA5 and, at the same time, receive frame 8'h5A on i_rxd (bits 65535 cycles each) with i_rx_ready=1. Then send two back-to-back transmit bytes with i_tx_valid held at 1.
checks.expected: Each o_txd bit lasts exactly 65535 cycles. o_tx_ready=0 for 655349 cycles and returns to 1 at E0+655349. The second back-to-back frame starts at E0+655350. 8'h5A is delivered with o_rx_frame_err=0 in the cycle after T0+32767+589815+2.

checks.title: Odd bit period regression, PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=7
checks.behavior: The design works for an odd N, where H=floor(7/2)=3.
checks.stimulus: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=7. Transmit and receive random bytes (back to back and with gaps), the sampling-point test, glitches of 1..3 samples and a 4-sample pulse, loopback.
checks.expected: Transmit bits last 7 cycles and o_tx_ready=0 for 69 cycles. Receive delivery is at T0+3+63+2=T0+68. Data samples are at T0+3+7(i+1). Glitches of 1..3 samples are rejected and a 4-sample pulse gives 8'hFF. Loopback delivery is at E0+69. All assertions pass.

checks.title: Full duplex independence
checks.behavior: Transmit and receive run at the same time with no effect on each other's timing or outputs. Same-cycle transmit handshakes and receive deliveries or takes are handled independently.
checks.stimulus: N=16. Run random transmit traffic (back to back and with gaps) and random receive frames at the same time, with random i_rx_ready, for 100 frames each way. Align some transmit handshake edges exactly with receive delivery edges V and with take edges.
checks.expected: o_txd and o_tx_ready match CHK-009/CHK-010/CHK-011 in every cycle. o_rx_valid, o_rx_data, o_rx_frame_err and o_rx_overrun match CHK-008 in every cycle. All transmitted bytes are correct and in order. All received bytes are delivered or dropped exactly as the model predicts at the same edges as in a receive-only run.

checks.title: Loopback o_txd to i_rxd
checks.behavior: Bytes sent are received intact with a fixed latency.
checks.stimulus: N=16. The testbench copies o_txd to i_rxd on every falling edge of i_clk. Send 8'h00, 8'hFF, 8'h55, 8'hAA and 50 random bytes, some back to back with i_tx_valid held at 1 and some with gaps. i_rx_ready=1.
checks.expected: For each handshake at E0 with data D: o_rx_valid=1 with o_rx_data=D and o_rx_frame_err=0 in the cycle after edge E0+H+9N+3 (T0=E0+1, V=T0+H+9N+2, H=8). No o_rx_overrun pulse. The received sequence equals the sent sequence.

checks.title: Asynchronous reset during transmission, release behaviour
checks.behavior: Reset asserted in the middle of a transmit frame abandons the frame at once. No byte is accepted during reset. The transmitter is idle and ready at release.
checks.stimulus: N=16. Hold i_rst_n=0 for 3 cycles at start with i_tx_valid=1 and random i_tx_data, then release on a falling edge of i_clk. Send byte 8'h00 by handshake at E0. At 5N+3 cycles after E0 (data bit, o_txd=0), drive i_rst_n=0 a quarter period after a rising edge (between edges). Keep i_tx_valid=1 and change i_tx_data for 3 cycles of reset. Release with i_tx_valid=0 and keep it 0 for 12N cycles. Then assert and release reset again with i_tx_valid=1 and i_tx_data=8'hA5 at the first edge R1.
checks.expected: During the initial reset, o_txd=1 and o_tx_ready=1 and no frame starts after release while i_tx_valid=0. Right after the mid-frame i_rst_n fall, before the next rising edge of i_clk: o_txd=1, o_tx_ready=1. During reset and for 12N cycles after the first release, o_txd stays 1 and o_tx_ready stays 1 (no rest of the abandoned frame, no byte from reset-time i_tx_valid). At the second release, a handshake happens at R1 and o_txd carries the frame of 8'hA5 starting in the cycle after R1 (bits per CHK-009), and o_tx_ready=0 for 10N-1 cycles.

checks.title: Reset during reception and between M and V
checks.behavior: A partly received frame is discarded by reset and gives no valid, frame error or overrun. The receiver is idle after release and receives the next frame normally.
checks.stimulus: N=16, i_rxd changed only on falling edges of i_clk. (a) Start frame 8'h00 on i_rxd. At T0+4N, assert i_rst_n=0 asynchronously between edges. Keep driving the rest of the frame and toggle i_rxd randomly for 5 cycles in reset. Set i_rxd=1 at least 1 cycle before a synchronous release, keep it high for 12N cycles, then send frame 8'h3C with i_rx_ready=1. (b) Receive byte 8'h11 with i_rx_ready=0 (held). Send frame 8'h22 and assert reset asynchronously at edge M+1 of 8'h22 (before V=M+2), then release with i_rxd=1.
checks.expected: (a) Between release and the delivery of 8'h3C: o_rx_valid=0, o_rx_frame_err=0, o_rx_overrun=0 in every cycle. 8'h3C is delivered with o_rx_valid=1, o_rx_data=8'h3C, o_rx_frame_err=0 in the cycle after V=T0+H+9N+2 (H=8) of its start edge. (b) Outputs are reset at once (o_rx_valid=0, o_rx_data=0). No o_rx_overrun pulse and no delivery of 8'h22 at any time after release; outputs stay 0 for 12N cycles.

checks.title: Reset while a byte is held
checks.behavior: Reset while o_rx_valid=1 discards the held byte at once.
checks.stimulus: N=16. Receive frame 8'hC3 with i_rx_ready=0 so that o_rx_valid=1. Assert i_rst_n=0 asynchronously half-way between two rising edges. Hold it 3 cycles, release synchronously with i_rxd=1 and i_rx_ready=1, and wait 12N cycles.
checks.expected: Before the next rising edge after the i_rst_n fall: o_rx_valid=0, o_rx_data=8'h00, o_rx_frame_err=0. After release, o_rx_valid stays 0, o_rx_data stays 8'h00 and o_rx_frame_err stays 0 for the whole 12N cycles. 8'hC3 never appears again.

checks.title: Line low at reset release
checks.behavior: The synchronizer resets to 1, so a low line at the first edge R1 after release is detected as a start bit at R1 and yields exactly one byte 8'h00 with frame error.
checks.stimulus: N=16. Hold i_rxd=0 during a reset of 3 cycles and keep it 0 after the synchronous release for 40N cycles, with i_rx_ready=0. Then drive i_rxd=1 for N cycles, take the held byte with one i_rx_ready=1 pulse, and send a normal frame 8'h5A.
checks.expected: In the cycle after edge V=R1+H+9N+2 (H=8): o_rx_valid=1, o_rx_data=8'h00, o_rx_frame_err=1. No other delivery and no o_rx_overrun pulse during the rest of the 40N low cycles. After the line goes high and then low, 8'h5A is delivered with o_rx_frame_err=0 at T0+H+9N+2 of its start edge.

checks.title: Basic receive, delivery latency, idle line
checks.behavior: Each correctly framed byte on i_rxd is delivered at V=T0+H+9N+2. A line that stays high delivers nothing.
checks.stimulus: N=16, H=8, i_rxd changed only on falling edges of i_clk, i_rx_ready=1. First keep i_rxd=1 for 20N cycles. Then send 8'h00, 8'hFF, 8'h55, 8'hAA and 50 random bytes, each bit exactly N cycles, with idle gaps of 1 to 3N cycles.
checks.expected: No o_rx_valid and no o_rx_overrun during the 20N idle cycles. For each frame with T0 = the first rising edge where i_rxd is sampled 0 after a 1: o_rx_valid rises in the cycle after V=T0+H+9N+2, with o_rx_data = sent byte and o_rx_frame_err=0. o_rx_valid falls one cycle later (taken at V+1). No o_rx_overrun pulse.

checks.title: Sampling-point test
checks.behavior: Data bit i is sampled exactly at T0+H+(i+1)N and the stop bit exactly at M=T0+H+9N. Values at all other edges are ignored.
checks.stimulus: N=16, H=8, i_rxd changed only on falling edges, i_rx_ready=1. For bytes 8'h00, 8'hFF, 8'h55, 8'hAA and 20 random bytes: s(T0-1)=1, s(T0)=0, s(T0+H)=0, and the start window holds 1 at all other edges from T0+1 to T0+H+N-2 except T0+H. For data bit i, the value is correct only at edge S_i=T0+H+(i+1)N and inverted at all other edges of its window (including S_i-1 and S_i+1). Stop bit: 1 only at M, 0 at M-1 and M+1, then 1 from M+2. Repeat with the stop bit 0 only at M and 1 around it.
checks.expected: Each byte is delivered in the cycle after V=M+2 with o_rx_data equal to the intended bits. o_rx_frame_err=0 when s(M)=1 and 1 when s(M)=0. The start detected at M+1 (s(M)=1, s(M+1)=0) is rejected as a glitch at M+1+H: no extra byte and no o_rx_overrun pulse. Any shift of the sampling edge by ±1 would invert the bits, so a mismatch means wrong sampling edges.

checks.title: Start-bit glitch rejection and acceptance
checks.behavior: Low pulses sampled at 1 to H edges starting at T0 are rejected with no output change. A pulse of H+1 samples is a start bit. After a glitch, a new start can be detected at any edge after T0+H.
checks.stimulus: N=16, H=8, i_rxd changed on falling edges. With the line high, apply low pulses of L samples, L=1..8 (s(T0..T0+L-1)=0, then 1), separated by 2N high cycles. Do this once with o_rx_valid=0 and once with a byte 8'h42 held (i_rx_ready=0). Then apply a pulse of L=8 followed by i_rxd=0 again at T0+H+1 for a full valid frame 8'h6B. Then apply a pulse of L=9 followed by line high.
checks.expected: For L=1..8: o_rx_valid, o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err do not change (8'h42 stays held) and o_rx_overrun stays 0. The frame 8'h6B starting at T0'=T0+H+1 is detected and delivered (or dropped with a pulse if held per CHK-008) at T0'+H+9N+2. For L=9 a frame is accepted: byte 8'hFF with o_rx_frame_err=0 at T0+H+9N+2.

checks.title: Back-to-back receive frames and minimal high time
checks.behavior: The receiver accepts frames with no idle bit between them. It detects a start one edge after the stop sample, needs only one high sample before a start bit, and delivers bytes in completion order.
checks.stimulus: N=16, i_rx_ready=1. (a) 10 random frames back to back: each stop bit of N cycles is followed directly by the next start bit. (b) A frame whose stop bit is high only at edge M (low from M+1 on, starting the next frame with T0'=M+1), followed by a valid frame 8'hE7. (c) After a low data period, a single high sample s(T0-1)=1 then s(T0)=0 starting frame 8'h19.
checks.expected: (a) 10 deliveries, each at its own T0+H+9N+2, i.e. exactly 10N cycles apart, in send order, all with o_rx_frame_err=0, no o_rx_overrun. (b) The first frame is delivered at M+2 with o_rx_frame_err=0, and 8'hE7 is detected at T0'=M+1 and delivered at M+1+H+9N+2. (c) 8'h19 is delivered at T0+H+9N+2.

checks.title: Frame error delivered, and frame error dropped by overrun
checks.behavior: A frame with stop sample 0 completes at M and is delivered with o_rx_frame_err=1 and its data bits, and is handled like any byte. If dropped, its flag is not reported.
checks.stimulus: N=16. (a) o_rx_valid=0, i_rx_ready=0: send 8'hB4 with stop bit 0 for N cycles, then line high for 2N cycles. Pulse i_rx_ready=1 for one cycle. Send a good frame 8'h4B. (b) Hold good byte 8'h12 (i_rx_ready=0), then send 8'h34 with stop bit 0, then take the held byte.
checks.expected: (a) In the cycle after V=M+2: o_rx_valid=1, o_rx_data=8'hB4, o_rx_frame_err=1, held until the i_rx_ready pulse. After the take, o_rx_valid=0 with o_rx_data=8'hB4 and o_rx_frame_err=1 kept. 8'h4B is delivered with o_rx_frame_err=0. (b) At V of 8'h34, o_rx_overrun=1 for one cycle. o_rx_data stays 8'h12 and o_rx_frame_err stays 0. After the take, o_rx_valid=0 and no byte 8'h34 and no frame-error flag ever appear.

checks.title: Overrun, and take at the delivery edge
checks.behavior: A frame completing while the holding register is full and not being emptied is dropped, with a one-cycle o_rx_overrun pulse. A take at V itself loads the new byte with no overrun.
checks.stimulus: N=16. i_rx_ready=0. Send 8'hA1 and then 8'hB2 (gap of 2N). Leave i_rx_ready=0 for 5N more cycles. Send 8'hC3 with i_rx_ready=1 only at its delivery edge V_C (driven high on the falling edge before V_C, low after). Send 8'hD4 with i_rx_ready=1 only at edge V_D-1.
checks.expected: After V_A: o_rx_valid=1, o_rx_data=8'hA1. In the cycle after V_B: o_rx_overrun=1, and it is 0 again in the cycle after V_B+1 with no i_rx_ready activity. o_rx_valid=1 and o_rx_data=8'hA1 are unchanged. In the cycle after V_C: o_rx_valid=1, o_rx_data=8'hC3, o_rx_frame_err=0, o_rx_overrun=0. In the cycle after V_D-1: o_rx_valid=0. After V_D: o_rx_valid=1, o_rx_data=8'hD4, no o_rx_overrun pulse.

checks.title: i_rx_ready patterns; receiver never stalls
checks.behavior: Receive timing does not depend on i_rx_ready. i_rx_ready has no effect while o_rx_valid=0. Bytes come out in completion order.
checks.stimulus: N=16. 60 random frames, mixing back-to-back frames and gaps, in three phases: i_rx_ready held at 1; i_rx_ready random each cycle; i_rx_ready held at 0 for 5 frames, then 1. While o_rx_valid=0, i_rx_ready toggles every cycle.
checks.expected: Every frame completes at its T0+H+9N+2: either loaded or dropped with a one-cycle o_rx_overrun (CHK-008 matches every cycle). In the held-0 phase, the first byte is held and frames 2..5 each give an o_rx_overrun pulse at their own V. Loaded plus dropped equals 60. Taken bytes appear in send order. Toggling i_rx_ready while o_rx_valid=0 changes none of o_rx_valid, o_rx_data, o_rx_frame_err or o_rx_overrun.

checks.title: Break (line held low)
checks.behavior: A line held low gives exactly one 8'h00 frame with frame error, or a drop with an overrun pulse. No further frame comes until a 1 then 0 is sampled.
checks.stimulus: N=16. (a) Line idle high, i_rx_ready=0, o_rx_valid=0. Drive i_rxd=0 for 30N cycles. Then drive i_rxd=1 for exactly one cycle and 0 again for 12N cycles. (b) Repeat (a) while a byte 8'h77 is held (i_rx_ready=0).
checks.expected: (a) Exactly one delivery: o_rx_data=8'h00, o_rx_frame_err=1 at T0+H+9N+2. No other delivery or overrun during the 30N low cycles. After the single high sample, a new frame is detected at the next 0 sample T0' and gives o_rx_overrun=1 for one cycle at T0'+H+9N+2 (the first break byte is still held). (b) The first break frame gives one o_rx_overrun pulse at its V, and 8'h77 stays held with o_rx_frame_err=0. There is exactly one pulse for the whole low period.

checks.title: Transmit data patterns with idle gaps
checks.behavior: Each accepted byte is sent as 8N1, LSB first, N cycles per bit, starting in the cycle after the handshake.
checks.stimulus: N=16. Send 8'h00, 8'hFF, 8'h55, 8'hAA and 50 random bytes. Each byte is offered with i_tx_valid=1 only until its handshake. Idle gaps between frames are random from 0 to 3*10N cycles, including 1 and N-1 cycles. i_rx_ready and i_rxd are idle (i_rxd=1).
checks.expected: For each handshake edge E0 with data D: o_txd=0 for cycles after E0..E0+N-1, D[j] for cycles after E0+(j+1)N..E0+(j+2)N-1, and 1 for cycles after E0+9N..E0+10N-1. o_tx_ready=0 for exactly 10N-1 cycles after E0. o_txd=1 during idle gaps. The sequence of decoded bytes equals the sequence sent.

checks.title: Back-to-back transmit with i_tx_valid held at 1
checks.behavior: With i_tx_valid held high, one byte is accepted every 10N cycles. Frames follow each other with no idle cycle, in acceptance order, using only the data present at each accepting edge.
checks.stimulus: N=16. Hold i_tx_valid=1 for 8 frames. i_tx_data takes a new random value every cycle, and the value present at each handshake edge is recorded.
checks.expected: Handshakes happen exactly at E0, E0+10N, E0+20N, ..., E0+70N. o_txd is a continuous stream of 8 frames: each stop bit (cycles after E0+10mN-N..E0+10mN-1) is immediately followed by a start bit in the cycle after E0+10mN, with no extra idle cycle. Each frame's data equals i_tx_data sampled at its own handshake edge, in the same order.

checks.title: i_tx_valid dropped before handshake and offers while busy
checks.behavior: Offers made while o_tx_ready=0 are not recorded. A valid that drops before a handshake sends nothing. A valid held until ready is accepted and sent exactly once. Only one byte is held.
checks.stimulus: N=16. Send 8'h96 at E0. During its frame (o_tx_ready=0), drive i_tx_valid=1 with i_tx_data=8'h0F for 20 cycles, then i_tx_valid=0 before edge E0+10N-1. Wait 30N cycles. Send 8'h81. During its frame, offer 8'h7E with i_tx_valid=1 held until the handshake. In the following frame, offer three different bytes in turn, each for 2N cycles, then drop valid before ready.
checks.expected: After the 8'h96 frame, o_txd stays 1 and o_tx_ready stays 1 for the 30N idle cycles (8'h0F is never sent). 8'h7E is accepted at the edge where o_tx_ready first returns to 1 and i_tx_valid=1 (the stop-bit end edge E0'+10N-1 sample of ready => handshake at E0'+10N), and is sent once right after 8'h81. None of the three bytes offered while busy is ever sent. o_txd=1 after that frame ends.

Elaboration error for illegal parameter values; not a simulation test.
The two-flop synchronizer structure is checked by lint/structural review. Its latency V=M+2 is checked by CHK-008 and CHK-023.
This binds the consumer. It is used as a stimulus choice (take before the next V) in no-overrun tests; overrun when it is broken is checked by CHK-028.
Environment rule: all tests release i_rst_n synchronously (on a falling edge of i_clk).
Environment rule: all tests hold i_rst_n=0 for at least 2 i_clk cycles at the start.
Environment rule: i_tx_valid, i_tx_data and i_rx_ready are driven on falling edges with no X/Z.
Environment rule: i_rxd is changed only on falling edges of i_clk, so s(E) is well defined.
Environment rule: i_rxd is always driven to 0/1 after reset release.
Timing closure at 50 MHz on GF180MCU; synthesis/STA.
All flip-flops use asynchronous i_rst_n; structural. Its port effect is checked by CHK-002 and CHK-019..CHK-021.
Storage minimality advice; nothing observable at the ports.

assumptions: s(E) means the value of i_rxd sampled at rising edge E of i_clk (before the internal synchronizer). This matches V=M+2, where 2 is the synchronizer latency, and the reference model computing s(E) from i_rxd.
'The cycle after edge E' is the interval between rising edges E and E+1. Port values at an edge are the values just before that edge. A handshake at E uses the o_tx_ready value just before E.
Tests without an explicit parameter use the default PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=16 (H=8).
The Section 8.5 loopback latency is not in the given rules. CHK-018 uses the latency derived from the rules when the testbench copies o_txd to i_rxd on falling edges: T0=E0+1, V=E0+H+9N+3.
PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=7 (CHK-016) is chosen as a representative legal odd value to cover the odd-N part of REQ-PAR-001. The full 4..65535 sweep is not simulated.
When reset is asserted after M but before V of a frame, the pending delivery is discarded (every flip-flop resets per REQ-RST-001).
